mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, leading to higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: GDP growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns are negative over the 60-day horizon in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 5% signals a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Unemployment rate remains below 5%, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the 20-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production indicates weakening supply chains, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Industrial production growth is negative, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate coupled with increasing unemployment rate signals monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% and UNRATE increases by 0.5%
failure_condition: Federal funds rate and unemployment rate both increase, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the 60-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong consumer demand in the housing market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: Housing starts increase, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the 20-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the consumer price index indicates high inflation, leading the Fed to raise rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: CPI growth exceeds 3% YoY, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the 5-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing retail sales indicate strong consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: Retail sales growth is positive, but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the 60-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment coupled with rising unemployment rate indicates labor market inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by 100,000 and UNRATE increases by 0.2%
failure_condition: Payroll employment increases and unemployment rate rises, but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of the 20-day windows.
